headline: State of the Flames: Craig Conroy on the rebuild timeline, the new arena and potential trade pieces
take:
The Athletic's State of the Flames piece has Craig Conroy talking about the rebuild timeline, the new arena and potential trade pieces. Conroy says he wants the team to be "competitive every night" while staying realistic about where the organization is on its timeline.

So far this season, our numbers say CGY is closer to that goal than a 4-6-0 record suggests. The Flames have taken 45.5% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality, not just shot counts), a below-even share but not a collapse, and 47% at five-on-five. Their results have run behind the process: they sit 5 goals below what their chances should have produced, and their goaltending has been 5.6 goals worse than expected, a stat that compares saves to the quality of shots faced. That points to bad puck luck and shaky goaltending, not just a weak roster. The special teams look middling, at 0.43 power-play expected goals per game and 0.73 allowed per game on the penalty kill. If the goaltending steadies, this team should win more than it has, and the "competitive every night" line looks believable. Any trade-piece talk will land on a team that is better than its record, with only 10 games of data behind that read.
